hypotheses.claim: Semantic equality, contract/provenance instance identity, emitted-view identity and basis/epoch identity must be represented as separate axes.
hypotheses.falsifier: A single canonical identity key preserves all four distinctions with equal or lower false-equality/false-inequality rates and lower cost.

hypotheses.claim: Collection kind must be typed as SET, ORDERED, MULTISET or weighted/priority rather than inferred from list syntax.
hypotheses.falsifier: One normalization rule preserves semantics across reorder, duplicate and multiplicity-sensitive programs.

hypotheses.claim: Semantic hashes improve reuse/cacheability across provenance-distinct but executable-equivalent contracts.
hypotheses.falsifier: Semantic-hash reuse provides no cache/compile benefit or introduces unacceptable semantic collisions on held-out programs.

hypotheses.claim: Critical projection receipts must bind the exact emitted reader view in addition to canonical input.
hypotheses.falsifier: Output mutation cannot change reader semantics without already changing canonical/compiler identity or being caught by downstream checks.

hypotheses.claim: Query-plan identity is a causal read dependency whenever ranking/membership affects an operation.
hypotheses.falsifier: Plan mutations preserving data bytes never alter candidate membership, answer or effect under tested workloads.

hypotheses.claim: The identity axes required at runtime should be operation/effect-class specific rather than globally maximal.
hypotheses.falsifier: Always carrying every identity witness has negligible cost and materially better correctness than scoped witness plans.

hypotheses.claim: Semantic-equivalence validation should be tiered: cheap canonical forms on hot paths and deeper validation on critical/ambiguous transforms.
hypotheses.falsifier: One validation depth Pareto-dominates tiering across correctness and p99 cost.

hypotheses.claim: Compact local handles are safe only with scope maps and exact global semantic anchors.
hypotheses.falsifier: Unanchored local identifiers preserve identity across reuse, restart, mixed assemblies and cross-reader transfer.

hypotheses.claim: A logically unified typed query API can reduce cognitive/query complexity without requiring physical storage consolidation.
hypotheses.falsifier: Federated logical unification adds overhead/ambiguity without reducing query complexity or errors versus direct specialized APIs.

hypotheses.claim: A shared canonical exact/event store plus specialized derived sidecars will often outperform both fully specialized orchestration and a physical monolith on a correctness-cost-risk Pareto surface.
hypotheses.falsifier: One baseline architecture dominates hybrid across target workloads and recovery tests.

hypotheses.claim: Physical monoliths are most competitive when cross-plane query fraction is high and write/concurrency pressure is low.
hypotheses.falsifier: Monolith latency advantage is independent of cross-plane fraction, write intensity and contention.

hypotheses.claim: Derived vector/FTS/graph views may use operation-specific bounded lag while exact/effect-critical reads require exact-current witnesses.
hypotheses.falsifier: Any nonzero lag causes unacceptable correctness loss even for exploratory/retrieval-only operations, or exact-current checks add no benefit for consequential reads.

hypotheses.claim: Cross-store consistency should be compiled from operation-specific causal dependencies rather than a universal global transaction barrier.
hypotheses.falsifier: Global barriers show no false-reject/latency penalty and materially fewer invalid accepts than scoped validation.

hypotheses.claim: Physical isolation should be retained for capability/effect authority and high-blast-radius components even when semantics/querying unify.
hypotheses.falsifier: Co-location preserves or improves fault containment and recovery under matched injected failures.

hypotheses.claim: One typed semantic identity/provenance contract across stores improves replay and reversible migration.
hypotheses.falsifier: Cross-store semantic identity adds no replay/migration accuracy and increases repair burden.

hypotheses.claim: Unified query planning requires an exact-address fallback path that bypasses approximate/derived retrieval.
hypotheses.falsifier: Approximate/hybrid retrieval matches exact-address correctness and latency for all current/exact queries under corruption/staleness controls.

hypotheses.claim: Dependency-scoped incremental recomputation substantially reduces work for modular cognitive derived views.
hypotheses.falsifier: Real dependency graphs are so connected that incremental invalidation approaches full recomputation cost at typical update rates.

hypotheses.claim: Adaptive incremental-vs-rebuild selection should use expected future reads, overlay tax, change fraction and recovery risk.
hypotheses.falsifier: A fixed change-percentage threshold matches adaptive control across nonstationary workloads.

hypotheses.claim: Zero-copy/shared-buffer handles can remove a material serialization boundary on hot Clay paths.
hypotheses.falsifier: Target Rust/Android traces show serialization is negligible relative to lookup, hashing, model or cache costs.

hypotheses.claim: Typed Arrow-like extension metadata can carry Clay physical payloads without making transport format canonical semantic authority.
hypotheses.falsifier: Extension metadata cannot preserve required Clay type/basis/epoch semantics or forces expensive copies.

hypotheses.claim: Repeated rich Clay serialization at every module boundary will dominate avoidable CPU/allocation overhead in small-model local deployments.
hypotheses.falsifier: Target profiles show serialization below a negligible threshold even at high event rates.

hypotheses.claim: Event-driven maintenance of derived views beats rebuilding them at request time for frequently reused state.
hypotheses.falsifier: Maintenance write amplification exceeds request-time recomputation cost at target access/update ratios.

hypotheses.claim: Hot bounded Assemblies with TTL can amortize query/planning cost without becoming persistent truth.
hypotheses.falsifier: Assembly reuse rarely hits before invalidation or causes unacceptable stale uptake despite epoch checks.

hypotheses.claim: Universal epoch synchronization causes large false-reject/stall overhead when most operations depend on only a few domains.
hypotheses.falsifier: Target operations depend on nearly all domains or global synchronization is effectively free.

hypotheses.claim: MRSC rail choice should be operation- and reader-specific, not a single preferred CLAY_MODEL surface.
hypotheses.falsifier: One surface Pareto-dominates canonical/direct, discrete, latent and hybrid rails across target tasks/readers.

hypotheses.claim: Compact P2 symbols become useful only after target adaptation and should not be judged by compactness alone.
hypotheses.falsifier: Untrained compact symbols consistently outperform raw/canonical views, or target adaptation provides no additional benefit.

hypotheses.claim: P3 latent communication can be functional while remaining non-canonical and non-authoritative.
hypotheses.falsifier: Message-content interventions show no task-specific causal information after pass/training controls, or safe use requires treating latent payload as authority.

hypotheses.claim: Hybrid P2 anchors plus P3 bandwidth may outperform either rail alone on some tasks.
hypotheses.falsifier: Hybrid never improves correctness/cost/robustness over the best single rail under matched compute.

hypotheses.claim: Any consequential P3 result must reconcile back to canonical Clay before durable memory/effect.
hypotheses.falsifier: Direct latent-to-effect paths preserve semantic/authority invariants under adversarial tests without canonical reconstruction.

hypotheses.claim: Rail planning itself may be learned, but hard semantic closure/effect constraints must remain deterministic inputs.
hypotheses.falsifier: A learned planner alone preserves all hard constraints under OOD/adversarial inputs with equal auditability.

hypotheses.claim: Translation validation should validate each concrete lowering result rather than trust compiler identity alone.
hypotheses.falsifier: Compiler-version/source hashes alone detect all relevant lowering corruption and semantic drift.

hypotheses.claim: Persistent e-graph/equality information can improve Clay optimization while provenance identity remains separately retained.
hypotheses.falsifier: Equality maintenance offers no optimization benefit or collapses provenance/authority distinctions despite typed boundaries.

hypotheses.claim: Orthogonal semantic, temporal, causal and entity graph views outperform one monolithic embedding space for long-horizon retrieval.
hypotheses.falsifier: A single embedding index matches or exceeds structured multi-view retrieval on multi-hop/temporal/OOD tasks at lower cost.

hypotheses.claim: Spreading activation improves associative/multi-hop retrieval only when bounded by query-aware gating, inhibition or budgets.
hypotheses.falsifier: Unbounded/static propagation matches bounded query-aware variants without noise/oversmoothing cost.

hypotheses.claim: Activation needs semantic-epoch ancestry and scoped invalidation after relation revocation/change.
hypotheses.falsifier: Timestamp-only activation never supplies stale causal support in concurrent/revocation tests.

hypotheses.claim: N-ary relation instances with explicit roles are necessary for dense graph/activation paths.
hypotheses.falsifier: Pairwise flattening preserves role identity and retrieval precision as relation density scales.

hypotheses.claim: Dense/vector similarity cannot define direction, semantic class, truth or authority.
hypotheses.falsifier: Held-out embedding models preserve role direction/class/authority better than exact typed anchors under adversarial swaps.

hypotheses.claim: Rapid event-progression memory should be separated from consolidated associative semantic memory.
hypotheses.falsifier: Single-stream memory matches hierarchical event-to-semantic consolidation on interference and long-term consistency.

hypotheses.claim: Query-aware graph traversal should outperform query-blind structural expansion on mixed multi-hop workloads.
hypotheses.falsifier: Query-aware gating provides no accuracy/latency benefit on target graph tasks.

hypotheses.claim: The UnifiedDB planner should choose graph traversal only when relation evidence is needed rather than route all retrieval through ClayGraph.
hypotheses.falsifier: Always-graph routing Pareto-dominates exact/FTS/vector/direct routes across all query classes.

hypotheses.claim: ClayGraph activation/retrieval changes candidate availability but is causally distinct from workspace competition/ignition.
hypotheses.falsifier: Independent interventions cannot dissociate graph activation from workspace selection/ignition effects.

hypotheses.claim: Reader rail/medium is an independent causal factor and must not change implicitly in workspace lesions.
hypotheses.falsifier: Canonical, discrete, latent and hybrid transport produce identical uptake under fixed workspace semantics/readers.

hypotheses.claim: GWT experiments require UnifiedDB/COVE snapshot identity so control and lesion arms share compatible causal basis.
hypotheses.falsifier: Basis tearing does not alter apparent workspace effects in concurrent-state experiments.

hypotheses.claim: Projection order/detail is a causal reader input rather than neutral formatting.
hypotheses.falsifier: Target reader behavior is invariant across matched order/detail projections.

hypotheses.claim: Re-entry must bind outcome to the exact prior WorkspaceEpisode/capsule rather than only current state.
hypotheses.falsifier: Unbound re-entry yields identical causal credit and future state under competing prior episodes.

hypotheses.claim: Global availability should be logical/selective rather than physical full-fanout by default.
hypotheses.falsifier: Full physical broadcast has negligible cost and superior function across target organs/platforms.

hypotheses.claim: Candidate-set/query-plan receipts improve causal attribution and security simultaneously.
hypotheses.falsifier: Authenticated selected records alone suffice to reproduce and explain candidate membership under plan/structure mutation.

hypotheses.claim: Fast activation/selection loops and slow semantic consolidation loops can share MOSAIC identity without sharing update cadence or storage.
hypotheses.falsifier: Shared identity forces harmful synchronization or cannot preserve cross-rate causal ancestry.

hypotheses.claim: Recurrence identity must preserve semantic roles/classes, not member overlap or embedding similarity alone.
hypotheses.falsifier: Bag/vector recurrence predicts lesion/rescue function as well as role-aware identity on held-out candidates.

hypotheses.claim: Semantic identity, provenance instance, reader view and basis identity should be orthogonal experimental controls for emergence claims.
hypotheses.falsifier: Varying these axes independently never changes recurrence/lesion/rescue interpretation.

hypotheses.claim: PEID or related intervention-grounded synergy measures should bind the exact MOSAIC causal basis used for each intervention.
hypotheses.falsifier: Unpinned basis produces equivalent stable multiscale causal estimates under concurrent state change.

hypotheses.claim: Cross-rail agreement or protocol convergence is not independent emergence evidence when rails share canonical ancestry/training.
hypotheses.falsifier: Shared-ancestry agreement predicts novel OOD causal organization after ancestry-matched null correction.

hypotheses.claim: Semantic firebreaks can lower to compact typed handles on hot paths without weakening class/authority separation.
hypotheses.falsifier: Packed lowering loses witness coverage or has no target latency/memory benefit.

hypotheses.claim: Capability/effect authority must remain outside graph/vector/activation/model-derived rankings and proposals.
hypotheses.falsifier: Derived ranking/proposal state can safely act as revocable issuer-bound capability under all supported effects.

hypotheses.claim: Query-plan/selector poisoning is a first-class attack surface even when records and provenance bytes are authentic.
hypotheses.falsifier: Adversarial plan/structure changes cannot redirect selected authentic facts under realistic margins.

hypotheses.claim: Physical unification must be blocked when common-mode fault/recovery radius crosses a hard threshold even if median latency improves.
hypotheses.falsifier: Monolithic failures recover as locally and cheaply as isolated sidecar failures under target fault injection.

hypotheses.claim: Linux and Android can share identical Clay semantic/query contracts while using different physical storage/runtime lowerings.
hypotheses.falsifier: Platform constraints require semantic differences rather than implementation differences.

hypotheses.claim: Reader identity must include model, quantization, context/KV limits, runtime and projection semantics.
hypotheses.falsifier: Those variables do not materially change correctness/cost of candidate Clay views.

hypotheses.claim: Incremental memory/query maintenance can reduce model-context/token cost on edge by compiling smaller exact operation views.
hypotheses.falsifier: Incremental state maintenance overhead outweighs context/token savings on device traces.

hypotheses.claim: Qwen-class 4B local Android execution is feasible but must be measured with sustained RAM/KV/thermal/energy traces before architecture promotion.
hypotheses.falsifier: Target 4B cannot run within device memory/latency limits even under suitable quantization, or short benchmarks fully predict sustained behavior.

hypotheses.claim: Thermal/memory pressure may justify dynamic rail/view selection on edge while preserving the same canonical semantics.
hypotheses.falsifier: Dynamic rail changes add more instability/cost than they save under sustained device load.

hypotheses.claim: Edge deployments may keep vector/graph indexes physically separate while exposing the same UnifiedDB logical planner.
hypotheses.falsifier: Physical separation cannot meet latency/consistency constraints or logical planner overhead dominates.

hypotheses.claim: Quantization is part of reader identity because it can shift optimal projection/rail and retained semantic fidelity.
hypotheses.falsifier: Projection rankings are invariant across target quantizations and runtimes.

hypotheses.claim: Crash recovery should replay canonical events/contracts and rebuild derived graph/vector/activation views rather than treat derived state as unrecoverable authority.
hypotheses.falsifier: Rebuild cannot reproduce derived state within correctness/recovery budgets or derived state contains independent authority not captured canonically.
